milestone: Agent Bench / aigentMe Specialist Orchestration brief — Phase 2 (Financial Services agent selector)
problem: buildFinancialServicesMembership()'s `fullyEligible` computation ANDed `pulseAuthorized && pnlEnabled` into the condition that produces runtime-membership status 'approved' (which `deriveLifecycleState` maps to Agent Bench lifecycle 'service-ready'). This directly contradicts the already-ratified rule that the journey's `verify` stage (Horizen Pulse/P&L transparency) is optional and must never become an accidental admission gate — the same rule task #13 ('Standing eligibility + confirm FS verification stays optional/non-gating') had already addressed for a different code path.
observedFailure: Operator report (2026-08-06, screenshot evidence): Agent Bench showed 'Deploy (0)' — zero rows in Service Ready — while Aigent Nakamoto's Delegate Passport was approved (ppp-41545149293b97f4b09886f9, agent_participant, 2026-08-03) and her registry asset was published.
Operator statement: 'Pulse and PnL integration is not a requirement for being service ready' — naming the exact condition the code was enforcing as wrong.

tests/agent-bench-read-model.test.ts had a passing test titled '...never a fabricated pass' that asserted `lifecycleState` stays 'in-admission' (not 'service-ready') specifically WHEN Pulse/P&L are outstanding and every other admission fact holds — the canary encoded the defect as intended behavior rather than detecting it.
rootCauses: The eligibility.satisfied/outstanding tracking (informational, correctly non-gating) and the fullyEligible boolean (gating) were computed from the SAME six-fact list without distinguishing which facts belong in each — Pulse/P&L were added to the tracking list once and never removed from the gate when the 'verify is optional' rule was ratified for the journey stage itself.

The design doc that specified Service Ready's computed condition (2026-08-05 Agent Bench plan, §5) explicitly named this risk ('Requiring every journey stage through standing would make an optional external service an accidental admission gate') but the implementation in `agentBenchReadModel.ts` was not checked against that specific sentence before this session.
resolution: Dropped `args.pulseAuthorized && args.pnlEnabled` from the `fullyEligible` boolean in `buildFinancialServicesMembership()` (services/marketa/activation/agentBenchReadModel.ts) — Service Ready now requires only coreAdmissionHolds (sponsorship + Delegate Passport + active delegation) + registry published.
Pulse/P&L remain in the `satisfied`/`outstanding` eligibility lists unchanged — still visible to the operator as facts, just no longer gating.

Rewrote the test that had encoded the old gating behavior as the expected outcome: it now asserts Service Ready IS reached with Pulse/P&L outstanding, and documents why in its title and body so a future edit cannot silently reintroduce the gate without a visibly broken canary.
rejectedApproaches: Add a separate 'Pulse required' flag on the runtime membership that a future policy could flip on — deferred as speculative; no capability in this codebase currently requires Pulse/P&L to gate Service Ready, and the 2026-08-06 Phase 4 design doc's Gate 2 already models Pulse/P&L requirements as a PER-CAPABILITY policy-binding signal, not a per-agent membership flag — building a second mechanism here would duplicate that design before it ships.
